title: "Experiment 2: curriculum benefit depends on pretraining"

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(afex)
library(Rmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(sjPlot)
library(tidyr)
library(ggh4x)
library(performance)
library(emmeans)
```

```{r define model functions, include=FALSE}
my_tab_model <- function(model){
  tab_model(model, 
          df.method = "wald",
          show.stat=TRUE,
          CSS = list(css.tdata = 'padding:0.1cm;padding-left:0.2cm;padding-right:0.2cm;'),
          transform = NULL,
          string.stat = "z",
          string.p = "p > |z|",
          show.re.var = FALSE,
          show.icc = FALSE,
          show.r2 = FALSE,
          wrap.labels = 100,
          show.ngroups = FALSE,
          show.obs = FALSE)
}

my_plot_model <- function(model){
  plot_model(model, 
          show.intercept = T,
          value.offset = 0.35,
          transform = NULL,
          show.values = T,) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = .5)
}

scale_this <- function(x){
  (x - mean(x, na.rm=TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm=TRUE)
}
```

### Loading Data
All continuous variables are z-scored
```{r read data, echo=T, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
pretrain_data <- read_csv("../data/exp2_pretraining.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
pretrain_data$trial_z <- scale_this(pretrain_data$trialNum)

train_data_curr <- read_csv("../data/exp2_learning_curriculum.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
train_data_curr$trial_z <- scale_this(train_data_curr$totalTrialNum)

train_data_ctrl <- read_csv("../data/exp2_learning_control.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
train_data_ctrl$trial_z <- scale_this(train_data_ctrl$totalTrialNum)

test_data <- read_csv("../data/exp2_test.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
test_data$trial_z <- scale_this(test_data$trialNum)

pretrain_data_smrt <- read_csv("../data/exp2_pretraining_smrt.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
pretrain_data_smrt$bin_z <- scale_this(pretrain_data_smrt$bin)

test_data_smrt <- read_csv("../data/exp2_test_smrt.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
test_data_smrt$pretrain_acc_z <- scale_this(test_data_smrt$pretrain_acc)
test_data_smrt$mean_sa_z <- scale_this(test_data_smrt$selective_attention)

learning_data_curriculum_smrt <- read_csv("../data/exp2_learning_curriculum_smrt.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
learning_data_curriculum_smrt$mean_sa_z <- scale_this(learning_data_curriculum_smrt$selective_attention)
learning_data_curriculum_smrt$trial_z <- scale_this(learning_data_curriculum_smrt$trialNum)

learning_data_control_smrt <- read_csv("../data/exp2_learning_control_smrt.csv",show_col_types = FALSE)
learning_data_control_smrt$mean_sa_z <- scale_this(learning_data_control_smrt$selective_attention)
learning_data_control_smrt$trial_z <- scale_this(learning_data_control_smrt$trialNum)
```

### Pretrain model
Does pretraining accuracy improve differently over time for the simple vs. XOR pretraining conditions?
```{r pretrain mod }
pretrain_mod = glmer(correct ~ pretraining * trial_z + (trial_z | subjectId), 
                  data = pretrain_data,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  pretraining="contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(pretrain_mod)
```

### Train model
Learning-phase accuracy for the control and curriculum groups, by pretraining condition and stimulus type.
```{r train mod }
train_ctrl_mod = glmer(correct ~ pretraining * stimType * trial_z + (trial_z * stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = train_data_ctrl,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  pretraining="contr.sum", 
                  stimType="contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(train_ctrl_mod)

train_curr_mod = glmer(correct ~ pretraining * stimType * trial_z + (trial_z * stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = train_data_curr,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  pretraining="contr.sum", 
                  stimType="contr.sum"))

my_tab_model(train_curr_mod)

```

### Test model
Does the simple-to-complex curriculum benefit at test depend on pretraining condition and stimulus type?
```{r test mod}
test_mod = glmer(correct ~ curriculum * pretraining * stimType + (stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = test_data,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  curriculum="contr.sum", 
                  pretraining="contr.sum", 
                  stimType="contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(test_mod)

# Overall STC benefit, averaging across pretraining and stimulus type
emm_overall <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ curriculum,
  weights = "proportional"
)

overall_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_overall,
  method = list(
    "STC - No Curriculum" = c(-1, 1)
  )
)
summary(overall_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# STC benefit separately for rules and exceptions,
# averaging across pretraining
emm_stim <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ curriculum | stimType,
  weights = "proportional"
)

stim_contrasts <- contrast(
  emm_stim,
  method = list(
    "STC - No Curriculum" = c(-1, 1)
  )
)
summary(stim_contrasts, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Overall pretraining effect, averaging across curriculum and stimType
emm_pretrain <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ pretraining,
  weights = "proportional"
)

pretrain_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_pretrain,
  method = list(
    "Simple - XOR" = c(1, -1)
  )
)
summary(pretrain_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Does the STC benefit differ by pretraining condition?
# (curriculum x pretraining interaction, averaging across stimType)
emm_curr_pretrain <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ curriculum * pretraining,
  weights = "proportional"
)

curr_pretrain_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_curr_pretrain,
  method = list(
    "(STC - No Curriculum | Simple) - (STC - No Curriculum | XOR)" = c(-1, 1, 1, -1)
  )
)
summary(curr_pretrain_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Overall stimType effect (rules vs. exceptions), averaging across
# curriculum and pretraining
emm_stimtype <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ stimType,
  weights = "proportional"
)

stimtype_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_stimtype,
  method = list(
    "Exception - Rule" = c(1, -1)
  )
)
summary(stimtype_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Does the rule/exception accuracy gap differ by pretraining condition?
# (pretraining x stimType interaction, averaging across curriculum)
emm_pretrain_stim <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ pretraining * stimType,
  weights = "proportional"
)

pretrain_stim_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_pretrain_stim,
  method = list(
    "(Exception - Rule | Simple) - (Exception - Rule | XOR)" = c(1, -1, -1, 1)
  )
)
summary(pretrain_stim_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Is the curriculum x pretraining interaction itself larger for exceptions
# than rules? (full curriculum x pretraining x stimType interaction)
emm_full <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ curriculum * pretraining * stimType
)

threeway_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_full,
  method = list(
    "(STC-NoCurr|Simple - STC-NoCurr|XOR): Exception vs. Rule" =
      c(-1, 1, 1, -1, 1, -1, -1, 1)
  )
)
summary(threeway_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Unpacking that interaction: is the STC benefit bigger for simple- than
# XOR-pretrained participants, tested separately within each stimulus type?
# (grid order for emm_full: NoCurr-Simple-Exc, STC-Simple-Exc, NoCurr-XOR-Exc,
#  STC-XOR-Exc, NoCurr-Simple-Rule, STC-Simple-Rule, NoCurr-XOR-Rule, STC-XOR-Rule)
curr_x_pretrain_by_stim <- contrast(
  emm_full,
  method = list(
    "(STC-NoCurr|Simple) - (STC-NoCurr|XOR), Exception only" =
      c(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    "(STC-NoCurr|Simple) - (STC-NoCurr|XOR), Rule only" =
      c(0, 0, 0, 0, -1, 1, 1, -1)
  )
)
summary(curr_x_pretrain_by_stim, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# STC benefit broken down by pretraining and stimulus type
emm_curr_by_pretrain_stim <- emmeans(
  test_mod,
  ~ curriculum | pretraining * stimType
)

curr_by_pretrain_stim_contrasts <- contrast(
  emm_curr_by_pretrain_stim,
  method = list(
    "STC - No Curriculum" = c(-1, 1)
  )
)
summary(curr_by_pretrain_stim_contrasts, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```

### Pretraining smrt
Does selective attention to the relevant feature grow relative to the irrelevant features over the course of simple pretraining?
```{r pretrain smrt}
pretrain_smrt_mod <- lm(SMRT ~ feature * bin_z,
                        data = pretrain_data_smrt,
                        contrasts = list(feature = "contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(pretrain_smrt_mod)

# Relevant vs. Irrelevant feature, overall
emm_feat <- emmeans(pretrain_smrt_mod, ~ feature)
feat_contrast <- contrast(
  emm_feat,
  method = list("Relevant - Irrelevant" = c(-1, 1))
)
summary(feat_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Does the Relevant - Irrelevant gap grow over the course of pretraining?
et_feat <- emtrends(pretrain_smrt_mod, ~ feature, var = "bin_z")
feat_slope_contrast <- contrast(
  et_feat,
  method = list("Relevant - Irrelevant" = c(-1, 1))
)
summary(feat_slope_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```

### Train model smrt
Does selective attention (compression) during pretraining predict learning-phase accuracy, for curriculum vs. control participants?
```{r train mod smrt }

train_curr_smrt_mod = glmer(correct ~ stimType * trial_z * mean_sa_z + (trial_z * stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = learning_data_curriculum_smrt,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e6)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  stimType="contr.sum"))

my_tab_model(train_curr_smrt_mod)
summary(train_curr_smrt_mod)

train_ctrl_smrt_mod = glmer(correct ~ stimType * trial_z * mean_sa_z + (trial_z * stimType | subjectId), 
                  data = learning_data_control_smrt,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e6)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  stimType="contr.sum"))

my_tab_model(train_ctrl_smrt_mod)
summary(train_ctrl_smrt_mod)
```

### Test model smrt
Does selective attention (compression) during pretraining predict who benefits most from the curriculum at test, controlling for pretraining accuracy?
```{r test mod smrt }
cor(test_data_smrt$mean_sa_z, test_data_smrt$pretrain_acc_z)

test_smrt_mod = glmer(correct ~ curriculum * mean_sa_z * stimType + pretrain_acc_z + (stimType | subjectId),
                  data = test_data_smrt,
                  family = binomial,
                  control = glmerControl(
                    optimizer = "bobyqa",
                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
                  ),
                  contrasts = list(
                  curriculum="contr.sum",
                  stimType="contr.sum"))

my_tab_model(test_smrt_mod)

# Overall mean_sa_z (compression) slope, averaging across curriculum and
# stimType -- proportional weights needed because stimType is unbalanced
et_overall_sa <- emtrends(
  test_smrt_mod,
  ~ 1,
  var = "mean_sa_z",
  weights = "proportional"
)
summary(et_overall_sa, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Does the curriculum benefit's dependence on mean_sa_z (compression) differ
# by curriculum condition, averaging across stimType?
et_curr_sa <- emtrends(
  test_smrt_mod,
  ~ curriculum,
  var = "mean_sa_z",
  weights = "proportional"
)

curr_sa_contrast <- contrast(
  et_curr_sa,
  method = list(
    "STC - No Curriculum" = c(-1, 1)
  )
)
summary(curr_sa_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# Is that curriculum x mean_sa_z slope-difference itself larger for
# exception stimuli than rule stimuli?
et_curr_sa_stim <- emtrends(
  test_smrt_mod,
  ~ curriculum * stimType,
  var = "mean_sa_z"
)

curr_sa_stim_contrast <- contrast(
  et_curr_sa_stim,
  method = list(
    "(STC-NoCurr slope | Exception) - (STC-NoCurr slope | Rule)" = c(-1, 1, 1, -1)
  )
)
summary(curr_sa_stim_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```
